# 3g Discovery, Phase 3 exit: contract

**Read first:** [build README → Phase 3](./README.md#phase-3-routing), [domain discovery](../processes/routing/domain-discovery.md), [catalog search](../processes/routing/catalog-search.md) (step 4 and its edge case: the Discover suggestion), [deployment](../deployment.md) (the `chromium` container), [architecture → outbound connections](../architecture.md#outbound-connections), `internal/modules/servers/ports.go` (`ProxyDialer`, `EndpointCatalog`) and `servers/proxy/dialer.go`, `~/projects/sh-blackberry/proxier.yaml`, designs `RP-Discover`, `RP-Search`, and the **As built** of 3a–3f and 1c (the xray dialer, its data race: routing tests never push XHTTP traffic).

**Done when:** the admin types a website and a discovery run queues (one at a time): it normalises the input, shows the catalog's suggestions in milliseconds, visits the site in a fresh headless Chromium context directly, through a chosen server (a per-run SOCKS listener on `ProxyDialer`) or **Auto** (direct, then through the first healthy server when the direct visit fails), with depth 0 or up to 5 same-site links, records every hostname with its failures and a screenshot per page, classifies them, and offers **Create custom service**, **Add to an existing custom service**, **Use suggestion** and **Visit again through…**; without Chromium only the lookup runs; runs and screenshots go after 30 days; the search page suggests discovery when nothing matches; the Chromium sidecar is drafted for blackberry; the Phase 3 exit demo is written for the user; every checklist line has its test.

## Decisions

| Topic | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Service | `discovery.Service` (Deps: DB, Events, Jobs, `Catalog`, `Services`, `Lists`, `Browser` (may be nil), `Servers servers.EndpointCatalog` (may be nil), `Dialer servers.ProxyDialer` (may be nil), `DataDir`, `Now`, Log). `Module.Discovery`. `Module.Browser discovery.Browser` (exported) is the real CDP browser when `PROXIER_CHROMIUM_URL` is set, else nil; tests set a fake before `platform.Open`. | Build README layout. |
| Input | `discovery.Normalise(input)`: trimmed; no scheme → `https://`; parsed as a URL; the host lowercased and turned into punycode (`idna.Lookup`); an IP or a host that fails `domain.Valid` is refused ("a website's name, like claude.ai"); the registrable domain by the public suffix list (`domain.Registrable`: `www.claude.ai` → `claude.ai`, `me.github.io` stays). The URL visited is the parsed one (path and query kept). | domain-discovery.md step 1. |
| Start | Form: **Website**; **Visit through**: Direct (default), Auto, or a server (the catalog port's active servers by name, the healthy ones selectable, the others shown disabled with their health); **Depth**: Home page (default) or Home page + up to 5 links. Without the ports only Direct. `Start` inserts the run (`queued`) and queues `routing.discover` (queue `discovery`, concurrency 1: a second run waits; 1 attempt; steps `lookup`, `visit`, `finish`; payload `{run_id}`), then the run page opens. | domain-discovery.md "starting a run"; "one run at a time". |
| Lookup | Step `lookup`: `catalog.Lookup(ctx, host, registrable)`; the suggestions are stored on the run (`running`) in the step's own `Write`, so the page shows them before the visit ends. Matching (current generations): a v2fly or iplist row whose name is the host as **exact**, the host or the registrable domain as **suffix**, or a parent of the registrable domain as a suffix (**above**). v2fly rows also name the lists that hold them through an include (the include graph with its filters): "also in category-ai-!cn, geolocation-!cn". Each suggestion: selector (spelled by 3c's rule), how it matched, the list's name count, and the service holding exactly that selector with its lists. Ordered: exact and suffix before above, v2fly before iplist, smaller lists first. | domain-discovery.md step 2. |
| Browser | `discovery.Browser` (interface): `Visit(ctx, Visit) (Result, error)` and `Version(ctx) (string, error)`. A `Visit`: the URL, an optional proxy URL, how many same-site links to follow (0 or 5), the registrable domain links must share, and the run's remaining host budget. Every visit path (direct, a server) is **one fresh browser context** (no cookies, no storage, disposed afterwards); its pages share it. Per page: navigate (90 s at most), wait until the network is idle for 2 s (at most 30 s), scroll to the bottom, wait 3 s, take a JPEG screenshot (quality 60, 1280×800 viewport), read the title; record every request (page, service-worker and websocket ones included): URL, host, resource type, status, redirect chain, and the failure text (`net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET`, `net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED`, a timeout). Then up to 5 distinct `http(s)` links of the same registrable domain, visited the same way. | domain-discovery.md step 3. |
| CDP | `discovery/cdp` implements it with `github.com/chromedp/chromedp`: resolve the configured host to an IP (Chrome's DevTools refuses a `Host` header that isn't an IP or `localhost`), read `http://<ip>:<port>/json/version` for `webSocketDebuggerUrl` and point it at that IP and port, `chromedp.NewRemoteAllocator(…, chromedp.NoModifyURL)`; per visit path `target.CreateBrowserContext` with `ProxyServer` set when visiting through a server, a target created in it, network events enabled, service workers through auto-attach (best effort). Its tests need a real Chromium and run only when `PROXIER_TEST_CHROMIUM_URL` is set (never in CI). | ADR 0001 (the sidecar is the only other process); architecture.md tech stack. |
| Through a server | `discovery/socks.Listen(ctx, peer, dial)`: a SOCKS5 server (no authentication, `CONNECT` only, IPv4, IPv6 and domain addresses, so names resolve at the server's end) on the local address that routes to the Chromium host (the local side of a UDP "connection" to it), on a random port, accepting connections **only from the Chromium host's IP**, relaying through `dial`. `dial` is `ProxyDialer.Dial(ctx, serverID)` (closed with the listener when the visit ends). The visit's proxy URL is `socks5://<that ip>:<port>`. | domain-discovery.md step 3.1; Chrome can't authenticate to a SOCKS proxy, so the peer address is the check. |
| ProxyDialer | servers' port returns `servers.DialFunc` (`func(ctx, network, addr string) (net.Conn, error)`, declared in the servers root) instead of `proxy.DialFunc`; its implementation converts. Routing then imports no other servers package (`TestImportsOnlyServersPorts`). Routing's tests use `routingtest.Servers` as the dialer (it dials directly and records the server), never xray. | Build README "Ports only". |
| Visit step | Direct: one visit. A server: one visit through it. **Auto**: direct, then, when the first page didn't load or any request of the direct visit failed, a second visit through the first healthy server (catalog port, by name); both are kept. Hosts are merged per hostname across visits: requests summed, `failed` = the direct visit's failure (first reason, and how many of its requests failed), `seen` = the visits that saw it. 300 distinct hostnames per run: the browser stops adding new ones and the run is marked `capped` ("Stopped at 300 hostnames."). Screenshots are written to `<PROXIER_DATA_DIR>/discovery/<run>/<visit>-<n>.jpg` (directory 0700) and named in the run's `visits`. | domain-discovery.md steps 3 and 4; Build README defaults (files, not rows). |
| Classes | `discovery.Classify(host, registrable)`: an IP literal → `ip`; the run's registrable domain → `first-party`; under a built-in tracker suffix → `tracker`; under a built-in CDN suffix → `cdn`; else `third-party`. The lists live in `discovery/classes.go`. CDN and infrastructure: `cloudflare.com`, `cloudflare.net`, `cloudfront.net`, `akamai.net`, `akamaihd.net`, `akamaized.net`, `edgekey.net`, `edgesuite.net`, `fastly.net`, `fastly.com`, `fastlylb.net`, `gstatic.com`, `googleapis.com`, `googleusercontent.com`, `ggpht.com`, `jsdelivr.net`, `unpkg.com`, `bootstrapcdn.com`, `azureedge.net`, `azurefd.net`, `msecnd.net`, `b-cdn.net`, `cdn77.org`, `amazonaws.com`, `yastatic.net`, `recaptcha.net`, `hcaptcha.com`. Trackers and ads: `google-analytics.com`, `googletagmanager.com`, `googlesyndication.com`, `googleadservices.com`, `doubleclick.net`, `facebook.net`, `hotjar.com`, `segment.io`, `segment.com`, `mixpanel.com`, `amplitude.com`, `sentry.io`, `nr-data.net`, `clarity.ms`, `bat.bing.com`, `cloudflareinsights.com`, `mc.yandex.ru`, `mc.yandex.com`, `top-fwz1.mail.ru`, `counter.yadro.ru`, `scorecardresearch.com`, `criteo.com`, `criteo.net`, `adnxs.com`, `taboola.com`, `outbrain.com`. | domain-discovery.md step 4. |
| Defaults | Ticked: groups of the first-party registrable domain, and every host that failed on the direct visit (with its reason). Not ticked: CDN, tracker, third-party. IP literals are listed apart and can't be ticked ("IP literals can't be routed (domains only): 203.0.113.5 · 1 request"). | domain-discovery.md step 4 table. |
| Finish | Step `finish`: classes stored, `done`, `routing.discovery_completed{website, hosts, suggestions}`. A visit that can't run (Chromium unreachable, a CDP error) fails the job: its `OnFailed` sets the run `failed` with the error and records `routing.discovery_failed{website, error}` (no `job.failed`); the suggestions stay on the page. A page that never loads is not a failure: its visit says so ("the page never loaded: ERR_CONNECTION_RESET"). Without a browser the `visit` step logs "Chromium is not configured" and the run ends `done` with suggestions only. | domain-discovery.md step 5 and rules. |
| Run page | `RP-Discover`: crumbs **Discover / run #41**, the host as title, the state ("finished · 16:31 · took 41 s · nothing changes until you save"), the line "https://app.example.com/ · visit through Auto · home page + up to 5 links · registrable domain example.com", **Visit again through… ▾**. Sections: **1 · Already in the catalog** ("found in 12 ms, before the visit"; each suggestion with how it matched, its count, "not a service yet" or its lists, **Use suggestion…**); **2 · Headless visits** (per visit: its path, a screenshot per page (`<img>` from the admin route), "loaded · 6 pages · 74 requests · 9 hosts" or the failure; "3 of 4 hosts failed · repeated through nl-1"); **3 · Pick what to route** (grouped by registrable domain: a checkbox, the domain "as a suffix", "· N hosts" expanding to its hosts with their own checkbox "exact, if picked alone", class, requests, failures on the direct visit, covered by ("anthropic in Main", `own.CoveredBy` over every list)); the IP literals line; the capped note; **4 · Save as a custom service** (name: the page title cut to 60, or the registrable domain; tag: its slug; routing lists with their targets ("Main · Home, iPhone"), the default ticked; **Create “Example” · 3 domains** (primary, `⌘↵`), **Add to an existing custom service… ▾**, the summary "example.com, example.net as suffixes", and "Saving goes through the normal checks: normalising, ownership, and the guard that refuses any domain covering a server hostname. Home and the iPhone config get it about 30 s later."). While the run is queued or running the page polls every 2 s. Keys: `space` ticks the cursor row, `↵` expands it, `j k` move. | ui/README discovery; `RP-Discover`. |
| Save | **Create custom service**: `discovery.Service.Create` normalises the picks into rows (the editor's rules), checks the guard over them for the chosen lists (`lists.CheckSet`; refused naming the server, as 3b: nothing created), then in one `Write` calls `services.CreateCustomTx` (3f; the service, its rows and snapshot, `service_added{origin: discovery}`) and `lists.AddTx` for each list (marked) → the new service's page. **Add to an existing custom service**: its rows plus the ticked ones through `SaveCustom` (the editor's normalisation and absorption, the guard) → its page. **Use suggestion**: `/routing/services/add?selector=…` (3b's page, lists ticked). Nothing changes until one of them is used. | domain-discovery.md "using the result"; "discovery never changes routing by itself". |
| Visit again | **Visit again through…**: Direct, Auto or a server: a new run with the same input and depth. | domain-discovery.md step 2 of "using the result". |
| Search hint | 3c's empty search result gains "Discover kinopoisk.com…" (a dotless query gets `.com`; a query with a dot is used as typed) linking `/routing/discover?website=…` (the form prefilled), with "opens a browser and lists every domain the site loads". | catalog-search.md step 4; Build README defaults. |
| Integration | `IntegrationDeclarer`: Settings → Integrations row **Chromium (discovery)**: "connected · HeadlessChrome/131…" (`Browser.Version`, 3 s), "not configured: set PROXIER_CHROMIUM_URL", or "unreachable: …". The Discover page says the same in one line. | 1c's integration rows. |
| Prune | The prune job deletes runs created more than 30 days ago with their directories (the directory first, then the row); a directory without a run is deleted too. | domain-discovery.md rules. |
| Nav | **Discover** `/routing/discover`, order 40. `SubjectNamer`: `discovery` → "run #41 · example.com", `/routing/discover/<id>`. | |
| Deployment | Drafted, **uncommitted**, in `~/projects/sh-blackberry/proxier.yaml`: service `chromium` (`chromedp/headless-shell:<the current stable tag, pinned>`, `restart: unless-stopped`, `cap_drop: ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, `mem_limit: 1g`, `shm_size: 256m`, `tmpfs: /tmp`, no ports, Dozzle labels) on a **new network `discovery`** (bridge, fixed subnet `10.89.251.0/29`, not internal: Chromium visits sites directly) that only `proxier` and `chromium` join, so the trusted-proxy subnet of the `proxier` network keeps the tunnel as its only other member; `PROXIER_CHROMIUM_URL: "http://chromium:9222"` on `proxier`. Checked locally with `docker compose config` and by running the image and reading `/json/version` by IP. `docs/deployment.md` describes it. | deployment.md; 2d's pattern for infra drafts. |

## Go signatures

### `routing/discovery`

```go
type Visit struct {
	URL         string
	Proxy       string // "" direct; "socks5://10.89.251.2:41234"
	Links       int    // 0 or 5
	Site        string // the registrable domain links must share
	MaxHosts    int    // what is left of the run's 300
	PageTimeout time.Duration // 90 s
}
type Page struct {
	URL        string
	Loaded     bool
	Status     int
	Error      string
	Screenshot []byte // JPEG
}
type Request struct {
	URL, Host, Type string
	Status          int
	Failed          string // "" or the failure text
	Page            int    // index in Result.Pages
}
type Result struct {
	Title    string
	Pages    []Page
	Requests []Request
	Capped   bool
}
type Browser interface {
	Visit(ctx context.Context, v Visit) (Result, error)
	Version(ctx context.Context) (string, error)
}

type Target struct {
	URL, Host, Registrable string
}
func Normalise(input string) (Target, error)
type Class string // first-party, cdn, tracker, third-party, ip
func Classify(host, registrable string) Class

type Start struct {
	Website  string
	Via      string // direct, server, auto
	ServerID int64
	Depth    int // 0 or 5
}
type VisitRecord struct {
	Path        string   `json:"path"` // "direct" or the server's name
	Loaded      bool     `json:"loaded"`
	Pages       int      `json:"pages"`
	Requests    int      `json:"requests"`
	Hosts       int      `json:"hosts"`
	Failed      int      `json:"failed"` // hosts with a failure
	Error       string   `json:"error,omitempty"`
	Screenshots []string `json:"screenshots"`
}
type Host struct {
	Host, Registrable string
	Class             Class
	Requests          int
	Failed            string
	Seen              []string
	CoveredBy         []string // "anthropic in Main", computed when read
}
type Run struct {
	ID          int64
	Input, URL  string
	Host        string
	Registrable string
	Via         string
	ServerID    int64
	ServerName  string
	Depth       int
	State       string
	JobID       int64
	Title       string
	Suggestions []catalog.Suggestion
	Visits      []VisitRecord
	Hosts       []Host
	Capped      bool
	Error       string
	CreatedAt   time.Time
	FinishedAt  time.Time
}
type Pick struct {
	Suffix []string // registrable domains of ticked groups
	Exact  []string // hosts ticked alone
}

type Deps struct {
	DB       *db.DB
	Events   *events.Catalog
	Jobs     *jobs.System
	Catalog  *catalog.Service
	Services *services.Service
	Lists    *lists.Service
	Browser  Browser                 // nil: lookup only
	Servers  servers.EndpointCatalog // nil: Direct only
	Dialer   servers.ProxyDialer     // nil: Direct only
	DataDir  string
	Now      func() time.Time
	Log      *slog.Logger
}
type Service struct{ /* … */ }
func New(d Deps) *Service

func (s *Service) Start(ctx context.Context, st Start, actor string) (int64, error) // store.FieldErrors
func (s *Service) Get(ctx context.Context, id int64) (Run, error)
func (s *Service) Recent(ctx context.Context, limit int) ([]Run, error)
func (s *Service) Create(ctx context.Context, id int64, c services.Custom, p Pick, lists []int64, actor string) (serviceID int64, err error) // *lists.GuardError
func (s *Service) AddTo(ctx context.Context, id, serviceID int64, p Pick, actor string) error
func (s *Service) Screenshot(id int64, file string) (string, error) // a path under DataDir, validated
func (s *Service) JobTypes() []jobs.Type // routing.discover
```

### `routing/discovery/socks`

```go
type Server struct{ /* … */ }
// Listen serves SOCKS5 CONNECT on the local address that routes to peer
// ("chromium:9222" or "10.89.251.3:9222"), accepting only peer's IP.
func Listen(ctx context.Context, peer string, dial func(ctx context.Context, network, addr string) (net.Conn, error)) (*Server, error)
func (s *Server) URL() string
func (s *Server) Close() error
```

### `routing/discovery/discoverytest`

```go
// Browser is a fake: each URL answers a scripted Result; Block holds visits
// until released; Fail makes the next visit fail like an unreachable Chromium.
type Browser struct{ /* … */ }
func New() *Browser
func (b *Browser) Site(url string, through string, r discovery.Result) // through: "" direct, or a server name
func (b *Browser) Block() (release func())
func (b *Browser) Fail(err error)
func (b *Browser) Visits() []discovery.Visit
```

### `routing/catalog` addition

```go
type Suggestion struct {
	Selector string
	Kind     string // list, site, group
	Portal   string
	Match    string // exact, suffix, above
	Name     string // the matching name in the list
	Domains  int
	Via      []string // v2fly lists holding it through an include
	Service  *services.Item
	Lists    []string
}
func (s *Service) Lookup(ctx context.Context, host, registrable string) ([]Suggestion, error)
```

### servers change

```go
package servers
type DialFunc func(ctx context.Context, network, addr string) (net.Conn, error)
type ProxyDialer interface {
	Dial(ctx context.Context, serverID int64) (DialFunc, io.Closer, error)
}
```

## Routes

| Method, path | What |
|---|---|
| `GET /routing/discover` | The form (`?website=` prefills) and recent runs |
| `POST /routing/discover` | Start → `/routing/discover/:id` |
| `GET /routing/discover/:id` | Run page |
| `GET /routing/discover/:id/status` | The filling areas (htmx poll) |
| `GET /routing/discover/:id/screenshots/:file` | A screenshot (`image/jpeg`, the file name validated) |
| `POST /routing/discover/:id/create` | Create custom service (`group=<domain>`, `host=<host>` repeated, name, tag, `list=<id>`) |
| `POST /routing/discover/:id/add` | Add to an existing custom service (`service=<id>`) |
| `POST /routing/discover/:id/again` | Visit again through (`via`, `server`) → the new run |

Recorded in 3g: `routing.discovery_completed`, `routing.discovery_failed`; the save actions record the services' and lists' events.

## Phase 3 exit demo

The user's, on the real deployment (the roadmap's exit: "`mtvpn.yaml` is imported. The home router's first sync is a no-op for unchanged services. The phone subscribes to the hosted Shadowrocket config instead of copyparty. Typing a new site finds its domains, and the router gets them within a minute of saving."):

1. Commit and deploy the sh-blackberry draft (the `chromium` service and the `discovery` network) and the image with Phase 3. Settings → Integrations shows Chromium connected.
2. Routing → Lists → **Import from mtvpn…**: paste today's `mtvpn.yaml`. In the preview check the rows (bare names written `v2fly:`, `tunneled-domains` as a URL source or copied into a custom service), the ignored keys, and the base box; import into "Main" with the config `iphone`. On the result page nothing mentions the password; Activity neither.
3. Shadowrocket → `iphone`: compare **What the phone gets** with today's copyparty file (the inserted block may differ where ownership now drops shared names). In Shadowrocket: Config → + → paste the URL → Use config; refresh it; delete the copyparty URL from the phone.
4. Routers → **Add router**: the home router. Install Proxier's key on the router with the dialog's `/user ssh-keys add …` (note whether it works on 7.24.5, or whether `/user ssh-keys import` of an uploaded file is needed: open question "to verify" 5), and on the jump host if one is used. **Test connection**, compare each fingerprint with `/ip ssh print` (router) and `ssh-keygen -lf` (jump host), **Save and sync**.
5. Open the initial sync's plan: unchanged tags are **recorded**, with no upload. Updates may appear only where ownership differs from what mtvpn installed (a name shared by two services now installed once); note them. The router keeps working.
6. Discover a site that isn't in any list (one blocked from home), **Auto**. Its domains are ticked; **Create** a custom service in "Main". Within a minute the router page shows a sync with one update; on the router `/ip dns static print where comment=<tag>` lists them.
7. Write the results into this contract's **As built**: what was recorded or updated at the first sync, the key command, SFTP, anything that differed.

## As built

Built 2026-10-09. `make check`, `make lint` and `docker build .` green; image 102 MB (chromedp adds ~9 MB).

**Packages.** `routing/discovery` (`Service`: `Start`, `Again`, `Get`, `Recent`, `Create`, `AddTo`, `Screenshot`, `Prune`, `Chromium`, `CanVisit`, `ThroughServers`, `Servers`, `JobTypes`; pure `Normalise`, `Classify`, `DefaultName`), `discovery/socks`, `discovery/cdp`, `discovery/discoverytest`, `catalog/lookup.go`, `store/discovery.go`, root `integrations.go` and `messages_discovery.go`, pages `discover.go/.templ`. servers: `servers.DialFunc`; `ProxyDialer.Dial` converts xray's.

**Deviations from the contract (each for a reason):**

- `discovery.Visit` has a `Path` field ("direct" or the server's name): logs, and the fake answers per path. `Deps.Peer` (the Chromium host's address) was added; `Module.ChromiumPeer` sets it, from `PROXIER_CHROMIUM_URL` in `Init` (`cdp.Browser.Peer()`), from `routingtest.WithBrowser` (127.0.0.1:9222) in tests.
- `Run` also has `Groups` (hosts by registrable domain, with the group's covered-by over every list) and `IPs`; `Host` has `FailedRequests`, `Tickable()`, `Ticked()`. The `failed` column holds `"<n> <reason>"` (no column for the count was written ahead).
- A third save path, `Service.Again`, for **Visit again through…**.
- `catalog.Lookup` returns one suggestion per selector (its best match); names between the host and its registrable domain count as the site's own. Groups of iplist aren't suggested (the reverse index holds sites).
- The screenshot is a 1280×800 clip of the document's **top** after the scroll (seen in the real browser: without the clip, the shot showed the page's bottom).
- The run page's state line is outside the polled area and is replaced out of band (`hx-swap-oob`) by each poll.
- Service workers' requests through auto-attach are **not** recorded (best effort in the contract; chromedp delivers other sessions' events elsewhere). Page, websocket and redirect requests are.
- "Found in 12 ms" isn't shown: the lookup's duration goes to the job log only.
- The pick count on **Create** follows the ticks through a small generic `proxier.js` addition (`[data-pick]` / `[data-pick-count]`); `↵` on a row with `data-enter` clicks it (a `<summary>` expands its group). The summary line of picked domains isn't built.
- chromedp **v0.16.0** (July 2026), not the latest: six releases came out in the week before this build.
- **The sh-blackberry draft** could not be written there: neither `~/projects/sh-blackberry` nor `~/projects/sh-main` exists on this machine. The compose snippet is in `docs/deployment.md#the-chromium-sidecar` for the user to put into `proxier.yaml`. Image pinned: `chromedp/headless-shell:156.0.8078.12` (stable on 2026-10-09). Its `/json/version` names it `Chrome/…`, not `HeadlessChrome/…`.

**Checked by hand, 2026-10-09** (Docker Desktop, arm64): the image with the draft's limits (`cap_drop ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, 1 GB, `shm_size 256m`, tmpfs) on a bridge network `10.89.251.0/29`; `docker compose config` of the draft; `TestRealChromium` against it; a Linux build of the discovery code in a container next to it: go.dev directly (6 pages, 288 requests, trackers `doubleclick.net`, `google-analytics.com`, `googletagmanager.com`, CDNs `gstatic.com`, `fonts.googleapis.com`) and example.com and go.dev through the SOCKS listener, peer `chromium:9222` (connections relayed, listener on 10.89.251.3). Then the real image (read-only, `cap_drop ALL`) with the sidecar, driven by a second Chromium over CDP: sign in, Search "kinopoisk" → **Discover kinopoisk.com…** → the prefilled form → a run of go.dev that polled to its end, `j`, space (count 1 → 0), `↵` (the group expands), space again, `⌘↵` in the name field → the new service's page; the run page at 390 px; no console error or CSP violation. No server exists here, so no visit went through a real server's endpoint.

**Left for the user:** the Phase 3 exit demo above, putting the compose draft into sh-blackberry, and a visit through a real server.
